record.paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
record.original_question: Does every complex cubic polynomial admit a square iterative root? Equivalently, if f is a complex polynomial of degree 3, must there exist a function φ such that φ(φ(z)) = f(z) for all complex z? The survey states that this basic existence question is still open even though quadratic polynomials are known not to have square roots.

evidence.quote: Even worse: we do not know whether every complex cubic polynomial has a square root.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An iterative square root of a function $f:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ is a function $\varphi:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ satisfying $\varphi(\varphi(z)) = f(z)$ for every $z\in\mathbb{C}$. (No regularity such as continuity, holomorphy, or polynomiality is imposed on $\varphi$ a priori.) It is known that there exist complex polynomials of degree 2 (for example, suitable quadratic polynomials) that admit no iterative square root in this sense.

Question: Does every complex polynomial $f$ of degree exactly $3$ admit an iterative square root? That is, given any $f(z) = a_3 z^3 + a_2 z^2 + a_1 z + a_0$ with $a_3 \neq 0$ and $a_i \in \mathbb{C}$, does there always exist a function $\varphi:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ with $\varphi\circ\varphi = f$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not turn up a definitive resolution of whether every complex cubic polynomial admits an iterative square root. Existing literature on iterative square roots (e.g., density results for continuous self-maps lacking square roots, and general results on iterative roots) does not appear to settle the cubic-polynomial case, and the question is described as open in surveys on functional equations in a single variable. No paper claiming a complete proof or counterexample for the cubic case was located.

status_evidence.title: Iterative square roots of functions — Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Continuous self-maps with no square roots are dense in the space of all continuous self-maps on cubes and on R^m.
status_evidence.claim: General results on existence/non-existence of iterative square roots exist, but they do not resolve the specific case of complex cubic polynomials.

status_evidence.title: Functional square root — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A functional square root of a function g is a function f satisfying f(f(x)) = g(x).
status_evidence.claim: Defines the notion of iterative/functional square root used in the problem; no entry asserts a resolution for complex cubic polynomials.
